answer: Each agent can earn nectar only by completing tasks that independent counterparties verify, with payouts delayed until a fresh network pulse confirms the receipts. The ledger binds each claim to a costly, nontransferable stake in shale-backed compute credits, which is slashed when audits expose duplicated identities or fabricated work. A sybil operator must therefore fund every persona and produce separately verifiable output; multiplying names alone earns nothing, while each failed identity burns its stake and compute budget.
